text:
sam_ae: Quick sync — Lumina wants a short validation run before the exec call. New ask: sustained ~600 rps with avg ~512 tokens, and up to 3x bursts at 1.8k rps for ~120s each. Deliverables: simple runbook, example load commands, quick hosted vs dedicated cost ranges, and a one-paragraph KMS/HSM latency note. Can we get this ready by Monday afternoon?

nina_sales: They also want a note about cross-region failover and brief SLA language (99.9% tail target). AE will float the initial budget range but wants a defensible cost delta.

omar_infra: Proposed approach: use k6 for arrival-rate control + our small metrics exporter to the console. Plan: 10m warmup @100rps, 10m ramp to 600rps, 20m steady, then 3 bursts 120s @1800rps with 8m spacing, 10m cool-down. Capture p50/p95/p99, error %, and token counters per minute.

omar_infra: k6 snippet (ramping-arrival-rate executor):
```
export default function() { http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', payload, { headers }); }
// run: k6 run --vus 0 --duration 00m50s script.js (config defines ramps)
```
(We put exact script in repo)

jess_eng: Perf notes from similar runs: for 512 tokens on rwd-30b-quant we saw p50 (stream start) ~140-220ms under steady batching, p95 ~430-700ms, p99 occasionally spiky if KV cache cold. For 600rps you should expect sustained GPU token throughput ~300k tok/s — plan for multi-pod pool.

jess_eng: Recommendation: run the PoC on rwd-30b-quant and one short calibration on rwd-70b-quant to show tradeoffs. Measure both stream-start and full-response end.

marta_sec: KMS note: envelope key unwrap is ~3-8ms per request under AWS KMS; inserting HSM-backed key management (dedicated HSM) typically adds 10-30ms depending on round trip and attestation. If Lumina mandates HSM/FIPS at-rest keys, that pushes us to private deployment or Dedicated with HSM integration and an addendum. I'll prepare a one-page summary for them.

billing-bot: quick-ballpark: Hosted consumption (per-token) for their expected PoC window (~1hr with bursts) ~ small hundreds to low thousands USD for PoC; sustained production at 600rps @512 tokens becomes material: suggest two options to present:
- Hosted (payg): simple, good for eval, but token spend scales linearly.
- Dedicated (reserved): sized pool (A100-style) for steady 600rps+burst headroom; rough reserved commit estimate: $30k-$75k/mo depending on instance family and batching. (I'll attach spreadsheet)

sam_ae: Nice. Can you give me the hosted rough numbers for the slide? Just a quick order-of-magnitude to avoid sticker shock.

billing-bot: Hosted rough: for 600rps * 512 tokens * 30m steady ~= 552M tokens -> at our public PoC price that's roughly $X00-$X50 for the window (POC). Production daily is the much larger number — we will put exact cells in the sheet.

omar_infra: Test run checklist (I'll run):
- Prep: auth token, k6 script in repo, targets + headers (X-Model-Variant).
- Warmup: 10m @100rps to warm KV cache.
- Calibration: 10m @600rps to ensure cluster sizing.
- Steady capture: 20m @600rps with metrics.
- Bursts: 3x 120s @1800rps spaced 8m apart.
- Post: gather k6 summary JSON, grafana p95/p99 screenshots, pod GPU traces and token counters.

sam_ae: Action items: Omar runs calibration Fri AM and posts results; Jess posts model-perf guidance + recommended GPU count; Marta posts KMS one-pager; Billing attaches spreadsheet with ranges. I'll update Lumina with tentative Monday 16:00 PT test window.

nina_sales: I'll prep the AE slide with the two options and a clear note: "POC shows viability; production requires committed sizing or throttling."

omar_infra: One more: use X-Model-Variant header and set streaming flag in payload to catch stream-start timing. Example curl (stream start measurement):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Model-Variant: rwd-30b-quant" \
  -d '{"stream":true,"prompt":"<test>"}'
```

nilling-bot: spreadsheet upload pending to this thread.

marta_sec: I'll also add the short audit CSV sample (encryption + key rotation columns) and drop it here by EOD.

sam_ae: Thanks all — keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
